edge_cases: Missing required fields in the JSON payload (e.g., title or year) may cause a server error
Providing a non‑integer value for year or book_id can lead to a 500 error or malformed query
Searching with an empty keyword returns all books (because LIKE '%%' matches everything)
Updating or deleting a book_id that does not exist results in a successful response but no rows changed
Very large input strings may cause performance degradation or exceed SQLite limits
Malformed or malicious input can trigger SQL injection due to string interpolation in queries
contract.intent: Expose a RESTful HTTP API that lets clients add, search, update, delete, and list books stored in a SQLite database.
invariants: All responses are JSON-encoded and include an HTTP status code (200 for success, 201 for creation)
Each book record is expected to have columns id (integer primary key), title (text), author (text), year (integer)
Database connections are opened, used for a single query, then closed for every request
The API does not perform authentication or authorization; any client can invoke the endpoints
io_behavior: POST /add_book with JSON {title, author, year} → 201 and JSON {"message":"Book added successfully"}
GET /search_books?keyword=… → 200 and JSON array of matching book rows
PUT /update_book/<book_id> with JSON {title?, author?, year?} → 200 and JSON {"message":"Book updated successfully"}
GET /get_books_by_year?year=… → 200 and JSON array of books from that year
side_effects: Creates or modifies the file library.db on the server filesystem
Inserts, updates, or deletes rows in the books table of the SQLite database
Opens a network socket to listen for HTTP requests while the Flask app runs
Commits transactions to persist changes in the database

rationale: The program implements all required routes with correct JSON responses and proper DB handling, preserving core behavior, I/O semantics, invariants, and side effects. However, it mitigates many listed edge cases (e.g., input validation, 404 on missing records, parameterized queries) rather than reproducing the contract's vulnerable behaviors, resulting in low edge‑case preservation.
